description: Just a guy exploring his tech skills to forward his climate ambitions
summary:
ESAMTA (Exploratory Seasonal and Annual Monsoon Trend Analyses for Maharashtra Region) is an Earth science analysis project focused on investigating precipitation variability, root-zone soil moisture, and potential drought conditions across Maharashtra, India, from 1998 to 2024.

Using NASA GPM IMERG Version 07 precipitation data and GLDAS Noah Version 2.1 land-surface model data, ESAMTA is designed to support statewide and district-level exploration of monthly, June–September monsoon, and annual environmental patterns.

The analytical approach uses Sen's slope to quantify long-term change and the Hamed–Rao modified Mann–Kendall test to assess trend significance while accounting for temporal autocorrelation. By combining regional visualization with transparent statistical interpretation, ESAMTA aims to make monsoon variability and potential land-surface drying patterns easier to investigate.

The application is currently under development, and final findings will be reported only after validating the complete data-processing and statistical workflow.
